name: Saphenous Nerve Entrapment
definition: Entrapment or irritation of the saphenous nerve, often in the adductor canal or infrapatellar branch, producing medial knee/leg sensory pain without motor deficit.

typical: Medial knee or leg burning pain

core: Motor exam to exclude femoral neuropathy

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is mainly clinical; ultrasound/electrodiagnostics or diagnostic block are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, tendon, cartilage, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent focal entrapment may require nerve specialist intervention.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu/Jangha Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Entrapment or irritation of the saphenous nerve, often in the adductor canal or infrapatellar branch, producing medial knee/leg sensory pain without motor deficit.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
